clue.text: Eagle observed following sound of tool for cheese

indicators.note: the sound of a word means we want a word pronounced like it but spelt otherwise

parts.note: a grater is the kitchen tool for shredding cheese
observed means seen, noticed, spotted

explanation.surface: An eagle seen just after hearing a cheese grater at work in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The greater spotted eagle is a large brown eagle species of eastern Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Call again with question of priest's identity

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest, and the 's stands for 'is'
it can mean the very thing itself, its identity, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Someone phones back to ask whether the caller is really a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev, is it?' is the question one asks to establish a priest's identity; 'question of' merely frames that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to visit or call on a place a second time.

clue.text: Say yes to a vice that's no end

indicators.note: a word with no end has lost its final letter

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: Agreeing to indulge a vice that seems to have no limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's no end' removes the D from GREED, leaving GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to assent, saying yes to a proposal.

clue.text: Model used to be more than enough

parts.note: ex means former, something that used to be
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A former model has grown more than adequately in size.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model to be copied or imitated.

clue.text: See 1
Request from 22

indicators.note: made from the letters of another answer, rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 22 down, whose letters are reused here

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference asking for something drawn from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to rearrange ELAPSE, the answer to 22, giving the six letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Please is the polite word of request, as in 'please pass the salt'.

clue.text: Terminals possibly used for doubles

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway or airport terminals might be built for double use.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis the tramlines are the outer strips of the court, in play only for doubles matches.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra side lanes on a tennis court come into play only when two-a-side games are played.

clue.text: Expand ancient site, removing top and installing home guard

indicators.note: installing means putting something inside the remaining letters
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, here taken away

parts.note: a henge is a prehistoric earthwork monument, like Stonehenge
a lar is a Roman household god, guardian of the home

explanation.surface: Plans to extend an ancient monument by stripping its top and stationing the Home Guard there.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's Second World War volunteer militia, a red herring here: the household gods of Roman homes were the true guards. 'removing top' and 'installing' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to make it bigger, to expand it.

clue.text: Manage after admiral beheaded in lighthouse by medical instrument

indicators.note: after places the word for manage at the end
in means the beheaded admiral is set inside the lighthouse

parts.note: the Pharos of Alexandria was the famous ancient lighthouse, and pharos means lighthouse

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the first letter

parts.note: Admiral John Byng was executed in 1757 for failing to relieve Minorca
to cope is to manage or get by

explanation.surface: Coping after an admiral was executed in a lighthouse, with a doctor's instrument at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Byng was shot on his own quarterdeck in 1757, so 'beheaded' only trims his name. 'in' and 'after' place the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharyngoscope is a device doctors use for examining the throat.

clue.text: Capsize vessel that's in full view?

parts.note: overt means open, plainly visible
an urn is a vase or container, a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat that capsizes in front of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something is to turn it upside down, to capsize it.

clue.text: Within range to hive off — put in a message

indicators.note: put in signals placing the rearranged letters inside the other words

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bee-keepers telegraph instructions to move a hive away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hive off' reads as splitting a business away, but 'off' just shuffles the four letters, and 'put in' places them inside the telegram word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achievable can be attained, so it lies within reach or range.

clue.text: Wordsworth's birth from 6

indicators.note: made from the letters of another answer, rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, whose letters are reused here

explanation.surface: A literary reference to the poet's birth drawn from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's Immortality Ode says 'Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting'; 'from' rearranges PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth wrote in his ode that our birth is but a sleep, so his birth is a slumber.

clue.text: Irish port and county first withdrawn after Scots one

indicators.note: after places the shortened county behind the Scottish one

parts.note: Ross, as in Ross and Cromarty, is a former Scottish county

indicators.note: first withdrawn means the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish port and an Irish county list after a Scottish one.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty was a Scottish county until 1975, so 'Scots one' means a Scottish county. 'first withdrawn' removes C, and 'after' sets the remainder last.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosslare is a ferry port in County Wexford in southeast Ireland.

clue.text: Operators keep time to fish

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: surgeons are those who perform operations

explanation.surface: Surgeons keep time before going fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeons are large fish prized for their roe, caviar.

clue.text: Cross about disgusted call for silence on way to ride

indicators.note: about means going around the other letters

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, a cross
ugh is a disgusted exclamation
sh is the call to be quiet

explanation.surface: An angry person reacts to a call for quiet on the way to go riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is the noun for a crucifix, and 'about' wraps it around the two exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride roughshod over others is to treat them harshly; it is the manner of riding.

clue.text: Foreign articles are not 10

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: A remark that foreign goods are not finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is OVER, so 'not 10' means the opposite of over.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of over is under, below in position.

clue.text: See 24
Relating to part of sentence left in one such

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a causal clause is one kind of clause, the part of sentence named before

explanation.surface: A grammarian notes that a part of a sentence was left in.
explanation.walkthrough: A causal clause, one beginning 'because', is one such part of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Clausal means concerning a clause, a part of a sentence.

clue.text: Policeman on beat for teenager on foot?

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman
to sock is to hit, beat

explanation.surface: A constable on his beat stops a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like the police round but is the verb to hit. Bobby socks were ankle socks worn by 1940s teenage girls, the bobby-soxers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle socks were worn by teenage girls in the forties, hence a teenager's footwear.

clue.text: Born king in scarlet (say) in place of rugs

indicators.note: in places the letter for king inside the heroine's surname

parts.note: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of Gone with the Wind, punned on scarlet

explanation.surface: A king born dressed in red in a carpet-making town.
explanation.walkthrough: '(say)' signals that 'scarlet' stands for Scarlett O'Hara, not the colour; 'in' puts K inside OHARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bokhara, now Bukhara in Uzbekistan, gives its name to a style of oriental rug.

clue.text: Parting word to encourage 10

parts.note: to cheer is to encourage
the digits 1 and 0 read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A farewell to encourage someone who is over ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 10 is not a cross-reference but the numerals read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, said at parting.

clue.text: Fall from 12

indicators.note: made from the letters of another answer, rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, whose letters are reused here

explanation.surface: A tumble drawn from another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or slips by, as one may say a period falls away.

clue.text: See 26
One even more likely to do a good 27, taking the high ground

parts.words: One even more likely to do a good 27
parts.note: a Boy ... does a good turn daily

explanation.surface: A boy who does good deeds climbs to the higher ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is TURN, the scout's daily good turn. Kinder Scout is the highest moorland in the Peak District of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This moorland plateau is the highest point of the Peak District.

clue.text: Put on reversion, having bounced twice?

indicators.note: reversion means turning the words back to front

explanation.surface: Reversing a put-on manner after a ball bounces twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis and squash a ball is 'not up' when it bounces twice before being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: In racket games the call for a ball that has bounced twice before being struck is this.

clue.text: One saint (male) taking flower, vegetable and pet to partially licensed house? You don't need to ask!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
he is the male pronoun
the Po is a river, so something that flows, a flower
a pea is a vegetable
a cat is a household pet

indicators.note: partially means only part of the word is used, its opening

explanation.surface: A saint with flowers, vegetables and a pet visits a pub; the answer is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' keeps LIC of 'licensed'. The Po is an Italian river, so a 'flower' in the sense of one that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhetorical question is a jokey retort meaning the answer is obviously yes.

clue.text: See 10
Second steps taken by detective in novel plant

parts.note: B is second, as in B-grade or the second letter
a ladder is a set of steps
Albert Campion is the detective in Margery Allingham's novels

explanation.surface: A fictional detective climbs a ladder briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladder campion is a wild flower with an inflated calyx, a plant of field margins.
